source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Primary neurocognitive decline with progressive memory loss as the defining feature of the cluster","B":"Odd or eccentric patterns, including paranoid and schizoid personality disorders in the cluster","C":"Anxious or fearful patterns, including avoidant and dependent personality disorders in the cluster","D":"Dramatic, emotional, or erratic patterns, including borderline and antisocial personality disorders"}}
source_row.rationale: DSM-based teaching traditionally groups antisocial, borderline, histrionic, and narcissistic personality disorders in Cluster B, often summarized as dramatic, emotional, or erratic. Cluster labels are descriptive groupings, not substitutes for individual diagnostic criteria.
source_row.source_detail: Current NCBI nursing text accessed 2026-08-14: Cluster B includes antisocial, borderline, histrionic, and narcissistic personality disorders and is characterized by dramatic, overly emotional, or unpredictable thinking/behavior.
source_row.source_name: NCBI Bookshelf — Personality Disorders (Nursing: Mental Health and Community Concepts)
source_row.stem: Which description best characterizes the traditional DSM grouping of Cluster B personality disorders?
